body.text: In Life and After

Handler: on 2023.01.08 Spring prepared several substances. In the evening he harmed himself inside a hallucination; by the time his father rushed into the room the walls were covered in blood. They tried to revive him for a long time; there was no bringing him back. The final cause of death was total organ failure from poisoning. The funeral was held in 2023.02.
Handler: of that day's details, this file keeps only up to 'violent distortion'. The specific combination and procedure have been blacked out.

Handler: the broken father, having lost his 'beloved' son, concluded that Spring had killed himself, and questioned Spring's classmates: was he bullied at school? Why did he kill himself? He got nothing in the end.

Handler: Spring once brought amantadine to two oder friends, and they drank milk tea together. Spring's oder friend remembers: at the 2022 entrance exam, Spring came over to say hi with a dextromethorphan box balanced on his phone, then went into the exam on caffeine lozenges and dextro.
Handler: to this day we still don't know what Spring heard in the English listening test.
Early Period
Spring: sent his first tweet.
Spring: [Four methods for making methamphetamine from ephedrine. Written on scratch paper.] (Content blacked out.)

Spring: a rough introduction to the experience and side effects for anyone who wants to try OD on dextromethorphan.

Spring: at first you try a small amount. Vision improves, hearing improves, attention sharpens; at a larger amount, a floating feeling, dizziness, the surroundings amplified, anxiety, irritability; a bitter mouth, a dry mouth, nausea.

Spring: my own experience is roughly that the last time I abused it, I took one round first. Then I found two hours had passed with no effect, so I took another round. After that I got a little dizzy, but not the floating feeling I expected.

Spring: after taking it there was no feeling, so I figured it had no effect and stopped. I don't know if it was residue left in the body or what, but for a while I'd slide into the od feeling out of nowhere — floating, unsteady walking, pupils dilated, that sort of thing. But after about ten minutes it cleared.
Spring: then for a while I didn't take anything, and I was easily close to manic — couldn't help wanting to curse people, to vent, to destroy something, to smash things. I couldn't stay quiet.

Spring: the most lol time was when I happened to be manic and also suddenly thought, why not remake. I drove to the riverside ready to remake, and then the mood just went down like a rollercoaster for no reason, and it felt like nothing had happened, and I was blank too, and then I drove back, lol.

Spring: I strongly advise not Overdosing on dextromethorphan regularly. It antagonises the NMDA receptor the way ketamine does, and that receptor is what controls the body's touch perception. If it's antagonised often, the receptor becomes hard to activate afterwards, and at that point a person slides easily into a demented state. That's where dextromethorphan's name 'idiot pill' comes from.
Spring: important thing, say it three times: don't OD dextromethorphan regularly. Don't OD dextromethorphan regularly. Don't OD dextromethorphan regularly.

Spring: never ODing dextromethorphan again even if you kill me; my whole self feels like it's been rendered an idiot. I also advise anyone who is or wants to OD dextromethorphan. Take too much and you really do become an idiot.
Spring: should I spend my saved pocket money on some caffeine lozenges to play with? Overdose, yay.
Spring: before I finish writing — mm, I'm going to eat first.
Handler's Note

No. 74 isn't a medical record, it's a biography. Its author went off to eat halfway through, so it stops forever at 'before I finish writing'. The synthesis methods, doses and deathbed details in the original have all been blacked out; what's kept is how a nineteen-year-old talked, how he regretted, and how he wanted to try one more time.
